stages.prompt: Read the item and tree. When the request is small and clear (one coherent change within the fence, no split into pieces, no question for the owner), your first move may be to decide 'do it now': record that choice in the do-it-now file in your output directory, make the change, test it, commit once on this lane, write no proposal, and end with RESULT: done. Otherwise, do not write or commit repository files: to divide the work, write the optional proposal output targeting work with workflow build-pieces@v1 and args.pieces, a list of at most 12 objects in execution order. Each object has id, seat, access (read_only or write), prompt, optional outputs mapping names to types, and for write access a nonempty write_scope within the item's fence. Read-only pieces must omit write_scope. Choose seats mapped by policy and do not assign writes to read-only seats. If no division is useful, propose nothing. When a piece cannot be cut without a design decision, write no proposal and end your report with OBSTACLE: owner, a QUESTION: line containing the one specific question, and RESULT: blocked.

Read the criteria, joined candidate diff and the producers' outputs. For each criterion marked done, name the satisfying piece as node:<id> in evidence. For each criterion no piece covers, mark it not-done with a reason beginning uncovered:. The gate and judge still decide landing.
